name: The Bellas household at 1634 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_bellas_t_h

present_on_scene_date.note: The household is listed at 1634 Prairie Avenue in both the 1904 and 1905 editions of the Blue Book, which bracket 1 July 1904, but not with the same people: the 1905 list prints 1634 Erastus Foote; 1634 Mrs. T. H. Bellas & dr.. Each person's own note says which of them the later list drops or adds.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1634, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 36, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The three live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. The daughters named in the 1900 census now have individual cards linked from the collective Blue Book entry. Their presence on 1 July 1904 remains uncertain. The 1910 census (T624 roll 241, ED 166 and 167) was read for this card's children: the children it lists, and those the Blue Book lists at the number from 1890 to 1911, are on the card with the years each lived here, whether or not they were at home in 1904. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: T. H. Bellas
persons.printed_as: 1634 Mr. & Mrs. T. H. Bellas & drs.
persons.note: The 1905 edition lists Mrs. T. H. Bellas & dr. without him, so his presence on 1 July 1904 is not documented. The 1900 census lists Thomas H. Bellas here as head, born November 1846, in Ireland, came to the United States in 1876, married, com. merchant (grain) (ED 36, sheet 2A, line 36, leaf n667).

born.note: The existing census transcription gives born November 1846. The year is carried into the age shown on this card.

portrait_research.note: An individual portrait has not yet been verified in the period portrait books and Glessner House Museum article archive searched for this project. Any figure shown is a reconstruction, not an attested likeness.

persons.name: The Misses Bellas
persons.printed_as: 1634 Mr. & Mrs. T. H. Bellas & drs.
persons.note: The Blue Book prints '& drs.' after the household's name: two or more unmarried daughters at home, neither named nor counted. One line stands for them all. 'Miss Bellas' is the book's own form of address, not a recorded name. The 1900 census lists the unmarried daughters at home as Emeline C. Bellas (born March 1881, in Illinois, single; ED 36, sheet 2A, line 38, leaf n667); Helen M. Bellas (born July 1884, in Illinois; ED 36, sheet 2A, line 39, leaf n667); Edith Bellas (born October 1887, in Illinois; ED 36, sheet 2A, line 40, leaf n667). Which of them the 1904 line stands for, the book does not say. The 1910 census lists the household under Erastus Foote, with Emma L. Bellas, widow, as his sister and Helena M. Bellas, 23, and Edith Bellas, 20, as his nieces (ED 166, sheet 9A, lines 1-4): very likely the daughters the book means.

persons.name: Erastus Foote
persons.note: Listed first at 1634 in both editions. The Blue Book does not say how he was related to the Bellases, or which of them headed the house; the card is anchored on the couple. The 1900 census lists Erastus Foote here as brother-in-law, born March 1850, in Maine, single, pres. iron works (ED 36, sheet 2A, line 42, leaf n667).

born.note: The existing census transcription gives born March 1850. The year is carried into the age shown on this card.
